content.value_statement: Azure Bot Service management can require many ARM SDK types and channel settings. This skill gives focused .NET examples for bots, channels, keys, updates, and errors.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup for Azure.ResourceManager.BotService and Azure.Identity.
Demonstrates authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and ARM clients.
Explains creating, updating, listing, and deleting Azure Bot resources.
Covers DirectLine, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat channel configuration.
Includes DirectLine key regeneration and RequestFailedException handling.
Lists key SDK classes, enum values, and official reference links.
limitations: Does not deploy or host the bot application endpoint.
Requires valid Azure permissions, subscriptions, and resource groups.
Does not replace production security review for bot credentials.
SDK versions and Azure service behavior may change over time.

use_cases.title: Provision Bot Resources
use_cases.description: Create or update Azure Bot Service resources from a .NET management workflow.

use_cases.title: Configure Channel Access
use_cases.description: Set up DirectLine, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat channels with appropriate properties.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Type Choices
use_cases.description: Map bot management tasks to the correct ARM SDK classes, constants, and enum values.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Bot Resource
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Azure Bot Service resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline how to create an Azure Bot Service resource in .NET. Include packages, authentication, resource group access, and required bot properties.

prompt_templates.title: Add Channel Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan channel configuration for an existing Azure bot. Compare DirectLine, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat settings.

prompt_templates.title: Maintain Existing Bots
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to describe a maintenance workflow for Azure Bot resources. Cover listing channels, updating bot properties, regenerating DirectLine keys, and deletion safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a production .NET ARM workflow for Bot Service. Cover managed identity, Key Vault boundaries, channel key rotation, error handling, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create a DirectLine-enabled bot in West US 2.
output: Install the Bot Service management and identity packages.
Create the bot resource with a valid endpoint and app identifier.
Enable a DirectLine site with secure site settings.

output_examples.input: Choose the right Bot Service enum values for a new production bot.
output: Use the Azure bot kind for current ARM-managed bots.
Choose the standard SKU when free-tier limits are not acceptable.
Prefer managed identity when the bot can use Azure identity controls.

output_examples.input: Handle a failure when creating a bot resource.
output: Catch Azure request failures from ARM operations.
Treat conflict responses as existing resource cases.
Log status, error code, and message for troubleshooting.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and grant only the Azure roles needed for bot management.
Keep MSA app credentials in Key Vault or managed identity-backed configuration.
Validate channel settings and bot endpoints before applying production changes.
anti_patterns: Do not place real client secrets directly in prompts or shared files.
Do not run update or delete workflows without confirming the target resource group.
Do not assume sample endpoints, app identifiers, or regions are production-ready.

faq.question: What does this skill help manage?
faq.answer: It helps manage Azure Bot Service resources and channels through the .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK.

faq.question: Does it create the bot application code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on management plane resources, not the runtime bot application.

faq.question: Which authentication approach does it show?
faq.answer: It uses DefaultAzureCredential and also lists standard Azure service principal variables.

faq.question: Which channels are covered?
faq.answer: It includes DirectLine, Microsoft Teams, Web Chat, and references for additional channel types.

faq.question: Can it help rotate DirectLine keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a workflow for requesting DirectLine key regeneration through the SDK.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with production bots?
faq.answer: Use it as implementation guidance, then apply your own access controls, testing, and change approval.
